title: Decidability of the nondeterministic tree-automaton index problem
formal: Is it decidable, given a nondeterministic parity automaton A on infinite full binary trees and a nonempty integer priority interval J={i,…,j}, whether some nondeterministic parity tree automaton over the same alphabet, using only priorities in J, recognizes exactly the same language as A?
definitions:
An input tree is a function from finite binary strings to a supplied finite nonempty alphabet Sigma. An automaton has a finite state set Q, an initial state q0, a transition relation Delta contained in Q×Sigma×Q×Q, and a map assigning a nonnegative integer priority to each state. A run labels every tree node by a state, starts with q0, and at each node obeys one transition specifying the left and right child states. A run accepts if, on every infinite branch, the largest priority appearing infinitely often is even. A tree is accepted if at least one accepting run exists. Missing transitions simply preclude a run.

All tables and priorities are explicit finite input data; i and j are binary integers with 0≤i≤j. The sought automaton may have any finite number of states and need not use every priority in J. Equivalence quantifies over all infinite Sigma-labelled binary trees. The decision algorithm is a total Turing machine with no complexity bound. The max-even convention is fixed for both automata; shifting or reversing priorities must preserve this convention and the target interval.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked decision procedure for all such inputs, or prove undecidability. A characterization with an undecided boundedness condition is insufficient. Results restricted to deterministic, alternating or word automata do not answer the nondeterministic tree problem.
context: The nondeterministic index measures the acceptance priorities intrinsically needed by a regular tree language. The 2025 paper supplies game and universal-tree characterizations while describing the general decision problem as open.
why: The index problem measures how much acceptance complexity is inherently needed to describe a tree language.

import_provenance.original_title: Decidability of the nondeterministic tree-automaton index problem
import_provenance.original_statement: Given a nondeterministic parity automaton on infinite binary trees and a finite priority interval J, decide whether an equivalent nondeterministic automaton using only priorities in J exists. This is an editorial continuation of Kupferman and Vardi’s work on transformations between acceptance conditions and tree-automaton emptiness.
